facts.t: The threshold fell from ₹1 crore to ₹3 lakh
facts.d: The 2015 Act set the specified value at a crore, confining commercial courts to large disputes. The 2018 amendment cut it to three lakh — a thirty-three-fold widening of access, and the single biggest change the Act has seen.

facts.t: Miss the 120-day deadline and you lose the right to defend
facts.d: Section 16 forfeits the defendant's right to file a written statement after 120 days from service. In ordinary civil procedure courts routinely condone delay; here the bar is absolute, and it is the Act's sharpest instrument.

facts.t: Only four High Courts have ordinary original civil jurisdiction
facts.d: Delhi, Bombay, Madras and Calcutta. The Act's two-tier design — Commercial Courts at district level, Commercial Divisions within High Courts — exists because those four courts try suits at first instance and the rest do not.

bank.q: The specified value for a commercial dispute after the 2018 amendment is:
bank.e: ₹3 lakh, reduced from the original ₹1 crore to widen access.

bank.q: With reference to the institutional structure, consider the following statements:
s: Commercial Divisions sit within High Courts having ordinary original civil jurisdiction.
Commercial Appellate Divisions hear appeals from both Commercial Courts and Commercial Divisions.
Every High Court in India exercises ordinary original civil jurisdiction.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Only Delhi, Bombay, Madras and Calcutta have ordinary original civil jurisdiction.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT within the definition of a commercial dispute?
o: Intellectual property disputes over trademarks and patents
Immovable property used exclusively in trade or commerce
bank.e: Matrimonial disputes fall outside the Act entirely. The definition covers ordinary transactions of merchants, bankers, financiers and traders.

bank.q: Consider the following timelines under the Act:
s: A written statement must be filed within 120 days of service.
Judgment must follow within 90 days of the conclusion of arguments.
Appeals must be filed within 60 days and disposed of within six months.
bank.e: All three are correct — the Act's design is built almost entirely around enforceable deadlines.

bank.as: Failure to file a written statement within 120 days forfeits the right to defend.
bank.rs: The Act prioritises certainty of timelines over the ordinary civil practice of condoning delay.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the provision is deliberately harsher than the general Code of Civil Procedure.

bank.q: Case Management Hearings are provided for under:
bank.e: Section 15A. Section 16 covers summary judgment and the written-statement deadline, and section 12A pre-institution mediation.

bank.q: All of the following are features of the Act EXCEPT:
o: Mandatory e-filing of documents and affidavits
A costs regime awarding actual costs
Summary judgment where no real triable issue exists
A statutory bar on appeals against decrees of Commercial Courts
bank.e: Appeals lie to the Commercial Appellate Division, within sixty days.

bank.q: What did the 2018 amendment additionally empower State Governments to do?
o: Constitute Commercial Courts at district judge level in ordinary original civil jurisdiction areas
bank.e: It permitted district-judge-level Commercial Courts even in areas where the High Court has ordinary original civil jurisdiction.

bank.q: Consider the following objectives of the Act:
s: Speedy disposal of high-value commercial disputes.
Improving ease of doing business through stronger contract enforcement.
Replacing arbitration as the primary route for commercial disputes.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Act complements arbitration rather than replacing it, and mandates pre-institution mediation.

bank.q: Which reform is proposed to extend the Act's reach?
o: Raising the specified value back to ₹1 crore
Establishing commercial courts in every district
Transferring intellectual property disputes to tribunals
bank.e: District-level expansion, alongside capacity building, digital integration and institutionalised pre-litigation mediation.
